translations.literal: From after the great flood of Wei Huangchu, the Yellow and Ji rivers overflowed; Deng Ai once wrote the "On the Ji and Yellow Rivers," opening the stone gate to connect them—to this point they were again inundated and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei’s Huangchu flood the Yellow and Ji had burst their banks; Deng Ai’s treatise and the stone sluice he opened had long held the waters—by now the works had failed again.

sentences.zh: 祗乃造沈萊堰，至今兗、豫無水患，百姓為立碑頌焉。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon built the Shen-Lai weirs; to this day Yan and Yu have no water harm; the hundred surnames erected a stele in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi built the Shen and Lai embankments; Yan and Yu have been free of floods since, and the people raised a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 尋表兼廷尉，遷常侍、左軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialed to concurrently hold commandant of justice, was promoted to regular attendant and general of the left army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added the post of commandant of justice, then became a regular attendant and general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，梓宮在殯，而太傅楊駿輔政，欲悅眾心，議普進封爵。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, while the catalpa coffin was still in the mourning shed, grand tutor Yang Jun directed the government, wishing to please the multitude's hearts, debated universally advancing noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor’s coffin still lay in mourning, Grand Tutor Yang Jun ran the government and proposed blanket promotions to buy popularity.

sentences.zh: 祗與駿書曰：「未有帝王始崩，臣下論功者也。

translations.literal: Zhi wrote to Jun: "Never yet has there been discussion of ministers' merits when an emperor has first died."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi wrote to Yang Jun, ‘No worthy court has ever handed out rewards for “merit” the moment an emperor dies.’"

sentences.zh: 」駿不從。

translations.literal: " Jun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jun ignored him.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 時將誅駿，而駿不之知。

translations.literal: At the time they were about to execute Jun, yet Jun did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The coup against Jun was already set, yet Jun knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 祗侍駿坐，而雲龍門閉，內外不通。

translations.literal: Zhi attended Jun seated, yet it was said the Dragon Gate was closed, inside and outside not communicating.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi was sitting with Jun when word came that the Dragon Gate was sealed and the palace cut off from the city.

sentences.zh: 祗請與尚書武茂聽國家消息，揖而下階。

translations.literal: Zhi asked to go with Director of the secretariat Wu Mao to listen for news of the state, bowed and went down the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi asked to go with Wu Mao of the secretariat to learn the court’s fate, bowed, and stepped down from the hall.

sentences.zh: 茂猶坐，祗顧曰：「君非天子臣邪！

translations.literal: Mao still sat; Zhi looked back saying: "Are you not the Son of Heaven's minister!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao remained seated; Fu Zhi turned and cried, ‘Are you not a minister of the throne?’"

sentences.zh: 今內外隔絕，不知國家所在，何得安坐！

translations.literal: Now inside and outside are cut off; we do not know where the court is—how can you sit at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: ‘Inside and outside are sealed—we do not even know where the sovereign is—how can you sit at ease?’"

sentences.zh: 」茂乃驚起。

translations.literal: " Mao then rose in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mao leapt up in alarm.

sentences.zh: 駿既伏誅，裴楷息瓚，駿之婿也，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: After Jun was put to death, Pei Kai's son Zan, Jun's son-in-law, was killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun fell, Pei Kai’s son Pei Zan—Jun’s son-in-law—was cut down by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射荀愷與楷不平，因奏楷是駿親，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: Vice-director of the secretariat, left, Xun Kai was not at peace with Kai, therefore memorialized that Kai was Jun's close kin and had him seized and handed to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice-director Xun Kai, who hated Pei Kai, memorialized that Kai was Jun’s intimate and had him arrested for the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 祗證楷無罪，有詔赦之。

translations.literal: Zhi testified that Kai had no crime; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi testified that Pei Kai was innocent, and an edict freed him.

sentences.zh: 時又收駿官屬，祗復啟曰：「昔魯芝為曹爽司馬，斬關出赴爽，宣帝義之，尚遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time they also seized Jun's subordinates; Zhi again stated: "In the past Lu Zhi was Sima to Cao Shuang, broke the gate bars and rode out to join Shuang—Emperor Xuan praised his righteousness and still promoted him to inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun’s staff were rounded up, Fu Zhi cited Lu Zhi, who broke out to join Cao Shuang yet was honored by Emperor Xuan with a Qingzhou post."

sentences.zh: 駿之僚佐不可加罰。

translations.literal: Jun's staff aides must not receive added punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun’s aides should not be punished further."

sentences.zh: 」詔又赦之。

translations.literal: " An edict again pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 祗多所維正皆如此。

translations.literal: Zhi's many upholdings of rectitude were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again Fu Zhi steadied justice in this way.

sentences.zh: 除河南尹，未拜，遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Henan; before investiture he was promoted colonel director of retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of Henan but before taking office was made colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 以討楊駿勳，當封郡公八千戶，固讓，減半，降封靈川縣公，千八百戶，餘二千二百戶封少子暢為武鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: For merit in striking Yang Jun he ought to have been enfeoffed duke of a commandery with eight thousand households; he firmly declined, halved it, was demoted in enfeoffment to duke of Lingchuan district with one thousand eight hundred households, the remaining two thousand two hundred households enfeoffed his youngest son Chang as village marquis of Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For crushing Yang Jun he merited a commandery-duke’s fief of eight thousand households; he refused until the court halved it to a district duke of Lingchuan with eighteen hundred households and enfeoffed his youngest son Chang as village marquis of Wuxiang with the remainder.

sentences.zh: 又以本封賜兄子雋為東明亭侯。

translations.literal: Further with his original fief he bestowed on elder brother's son Jun village marquis of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: From his original grant he also made his nephew Jun village marquis of Dongming.

sentences.zh: 楚王瑋之矯詔也，祗以聞奏稽留，免官。

translations.literal: When Prince Chu, Wei, forged the edict, Zhi because reporting was delayed was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chu, Sima Wei, forged an edict, Fu Zhi was dismissed for slow reporting.

sentences.zh: 期年，遷光祿勳，復以公事免。

translations.literal: After a full year he was promoted grand master of splendid horses; again for public affairs he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became grand master of splendid horses, then was removed again over a public affair.

sentences.zh: 氐人齊萬年舉兵反，以祗為行安西軍司，加常侍，率安西將軍夏侯駿討平之。

translations.literal: The Di man Qi Wannian raised troops in revolt; Zhi was made acting commander of the army of the west of peace, with concurrent regular attendant, leading general of the west who pacifies the wilderness Xiahou Jun to strike and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di leader Qi Wannian rebelled, Fu Zhi served as acting chief of staff for the Army of the West with concurrent regular attendant, accompanying General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 遷衛尉，以風疾遜位，就拜常侍，食卿祿秩，賜錢及床帳等。

translations.literal: He was promoted commandant of the guards, on wind illness yielded place, was then appointed regular attendant, ate ministerial salary ranks, was granted cash, bed-curtains, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted commandant of the guards, he resigned with a palsy, was kept as regular attendant on ministerial salary, and given cash, bedding, and the like.

sentences.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was added grand counsellor of splendid horses; mounted patrol lanes were set up at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added the title grand counsellor of splendid horses and was allowed the mounted patrol barrier at his gate.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫輔政，以為中書監，常侍如故，以鎮眾心。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao, Lun, directed the government, he made him overseer of the secretariat, regular attendant as before, to steady the host of hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, took charge, he made Fu Zhi overseer of the secretariat, still a regular attendant, to calm public opinion.

sentences.zh: 祗辭之以疾，倫遣御史輿祗就職。

translations.literal: Zhi declined on grounds of illness; Lun sent a censor to carry Zhi in a litter to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi pleaded illness; Lun sent a censor with a litter to force him to his desk.

sentences.zh: 王戎、陳准等相與言曰：「傅公在事，吾屬無憂矣。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, Chen Zhun, and others spoke together: "With Lord Fu in charge, our sort has no worries.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong and Chen Zhun said to each other, ‘With Lord Fu at the helm we need not worry.’"

sentences.zh: 」其為物所倚信如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he was trusted by others to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the trust men placed in him.

sentences.zh: 倫篡，又為右光祿、開府，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped, he again was right grand master of splendid horses, established office, added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun seized the throne, Fu Zhi became right grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment and added palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 惠帝還宮，祗以經受偽職請退，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui returned to the palace, Zhi because he had received illicit office asked to retire—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui returned, Fu Zhi asked to resign for having served the usurper; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 初，倫之篡也，孫秀與義陽王威等十餘人預撰儀式禪文。

translations.literal: At first when Lun usurped, Sun Xiu and Prince of Yiyang, Wei, and more than a dozen others pre-drafted the ceremonies and abdication texts.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun first usurped, Sun Xiu, Prince Yiyang Sima Wei, and a dozen others had drafted the abdication liturgy and text.

sentences.zh: 及倫敗，齊王冏收侍中劉逵、常侍騶捷、杜育、黃門郎陸機、右丞周導、王尊等付廷尉。

translations.literal: When Lun fell, the prince of Qi, Jiong, seized palace attendant Liu Dai, regular attendants Zou Jie, Du Yu, yellow gate gentleman Lu Ji, right aide Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others and handed them to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun fell, Prince Qi Sima Jiong arrested Liu Dai, Zou Jie, Du Yu, Lu Ji, Zhou Dao, Wang Zun, and others for the commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 以禪文出中書，復議處祗罪，會赦得原。

translations.literal: Because the abdication text came from the secretariat, they again debated punishing Zhi's crime, but a general amnesty arrived and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because the abdication edict had issued from the secretariat, some wanted Fu Zhi punished, but a general amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後以禪文草本非祗所撰，於是詔復光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later because the abdication draft in manuscript was not written by Zhi, thereupon an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was shown the draft was not his hand, and an edict restored him as grand counsellor of splendid horses.

sentences.zh: 子宣，尚弘農公主。

translations.literal: His son Xuan married the Princess of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Xuan married the princess of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子少傅，上章遜位還第。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted junior tutor to the heir apparent; he submitted a memorial yielding office and returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became junior tutor to the heir apparent, then begged leave to retire home.

sentences.zh: 及成都王穎為太傅，復以祗為少傅，加侍中。

translations.literal: When Prince Chengdu, Ying, was grand tutor, again he made Zhi junior tutor, added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chengdu Sima Ying became grand tutor, he again named Fu Zhi junior tutor with added palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，遷光祿大夫、侍中，未拜，加右僕射、中書監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was promoted grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant; before investiture he was added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he rose to grand counsellor of splendid horses and palace attendant, then—before the first appointment took effect—added right vice-director and overseer of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時太傅東海王越輔政，祗既居端右，每宣君臣謙光之道，由此上下雍穆。

translations.literal: At that time grand tutor Prince of Donghai Yue directed the government; Zhi already stood at the head of the right—often he proclaimed the way of ruler and ministers yielding glory, and thereby above and below were harmonious and reverent.
translations.idiomatic: While Grand Tutor Prince Donghai Sima Yue governed, Fu Zhi as senior minister on the right preached mutual deference between sovereign and ministers, and court relations grew calm.

sentences.zh: 祗明達國體，朝廷制度多所經綜。

translations.literal: Zhi understood the state's body; many court systems he had managed and drawn together.
translations.idiomatic: He grasped how the state should run and had shaped many of its institutions.

sentences.zh: 曆左光祿、開府，行太子太傅，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He served as left grand master of splendid horses, established office, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, palace attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through left grand master of splendid horses with independent establishment, acting grand tutor to the heir apparent, still a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 疾篤遜位，不許。

translations.literal: On grave illness he yielded office—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, he asked to retire; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒，以足疾，詔版輿上殿，不拜。

translations.literal: He was promoted minister of education; on foot ailment an edict ordered a litter to the hall; he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to minister of education, he was carried in a litter to court because of his feet and excused from bowing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍苟晞表請遷都，使祗出詣河陰，修理舟楫，為水行之備。

translations.literal: Great general Gou Xi memorialized requesting removal of the capital, sent Zhi out to Heyin to repair boats and oars, preparing for travel by water.
translations.idiomatic: General Gou Xi proposed moving the capital and sent Fu Zhi to Heyin to ready boats for a river retreat.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷沒，遂共建行台，推祗為盟主，以司徒、持節、大都督諸軍事傳檄四方。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell and was lost, they thereupon jointly set up a mobile headquarters, pushed Zhi to be covenant lord, transmitting proclamations in the four directions as minister of education, bearer of the staff of authority, grand governor of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, the exiles set up a mobile command, chose Fu Zhi as their head, and issued calls in his name as minister of education, credential-bearing supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 遣子宣將公主與尚書令和郁赴告方伯征義兵，祗自屯盟津小城，宣弟暢行河陰令，以待宣。

translations.literal: He sent son Xuan leading the princess and Director of the secretariat He Yu to notify regional governors and summon righteous troops; Zhi himself camped at the small fort of Meng Ford; Xuan's younger brother Chang acted as magistrate of Heyin to await Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Xuan with the princess and He Yu, the director of the secretariat, to rally regional lords while he himself held the small fort at Meng Ford; his younger son Chang served as magistrate of Heyin to cover the crossing.

sentences.zh: 祗以暴疾薨，時年六十九。

translations.literal: Zhi died of sudden illness at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi died of a sudden illness at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 祗自以義誠不終，力疾手筆敕厲其二子宣、暢，辭旨深切，覽者莫不感激慷慨。

translations.literal: Zhi himself thought his obligation of loyalty unfinished; with force of sickness he personally wrote in brush stern admonition to his two sons Xuan and Chang; the wording was bitter and deep, none who read it failed to be moved and roused.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his duty of loyalty unfinished, he dragged himself from his sickbed to write a fierce testament for Xuan and Chang; every reader was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 祗著文章駁論十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Zhi authored refutation essays of over a hundred thousand graphs.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a hundred thousand characters of essays and polemics.

sentences.zh: 宣字世弘。

translations.literal: Xuan's style name was Shihong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Shihong.

sentences.zh: 年六歲喪繼母，哭泣如成人，中表異之。

translations.literal: At age six he lost his stepmother; he wept like an adult, and cousins marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At six he lost his stepmother and wept like a grown man; kinsfolk marveled.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，趙王倫以為相國掾、尚書郎、太子中舍人，遷司徒西曹掾。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, gentleman of the secretariat, palace gentleman to the heir apparent; he was promoted aide in the western bureau of the minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he loved books; Prince Zhao Lun made him aide to the minister of state, secretary, heir’s gentleman, then aide in the minister of education’s western bureau.

sentences.zh: 去職，累遷為秘書丞、驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: Leaving office, by stages he was promoted secretary assistant, aide-de-camp on the staff of the general who gallops to battle.
translations.idiomatic: After resigning he rose to secretary’s aide and staff officer to the general who gallops to battle.

sentences.zh: 惠帝至自長安，以宣為左丞，不就，遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang-an, Xuan was made left aide—he did not take office—and was promoted gentleman at the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui returned from Chang’an, Fu Xuan was named left aide but declined, then was made gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，轉吏部郎，又為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai mounted the throne, he was transferred to gentleman of the ministry of personnel, again became metropolitan censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he became a gentleman in the ministry of personnel, then metropolitan censor again.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十九，無子，以暢子沖為嗣。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-nine, without sons; Chang's son Chong was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine without a son, so his brother Chang’s son Chong inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 暢字世道。

translations.literal: Chang's style name was Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang, courtesy name Shidao.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，父友見而戲之，解暢衣，取其金環與侍者，暢不之惜，以此賞之。

translations.literal: At age five, a friend of his father saw him and teased him, stripped Chang's clothes, took his gold ring and gave it to a servant—Chang did not grudge it; for this they praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five, a friend of his father teased him, stripped off his coat, and gave his gold ring to a servant; the boy showed no resentment, and adults praised his composure.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，甚有重名。

translations.literal: Before the capping year he already had great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he was already famous.

sentences.zh: 以選入侍講東宮，為秘書丞。

translations.literal: By selection he entered to lecture in the eastern palace, became secretary assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for the heir’s lecture staff, he became an assistant in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 尋沒于石勒，勒以為大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was lost to Shi Le; Le made him major on the right to the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell into Shi Le’s hands; Le appointed him senior clerk on the right for the grand general.

sentences.zh: 諳識朝儀，恆居機密，勒甚重之。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in court ceremony, he always dwelt in secret matters; Le greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Expert in court ritual and privy to every secret plan, he won Shi Le’s deep respect.

sentences.zh: 作《晉諸公敘贊》二十二卷，又為《公卿故事》九卷。

translations.literal: He composed *Appraisal Narratives of Jin Lords* in twenty-two fascicles, also *Stories of Dukes and Ministers* in nine fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the *Appraisal Narratives of Jin Lords* in twenty-two scrolls and the *Stories of Dukes and Ministers* in nine.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子詠，過江為交州刺史、太子右率。

translations.literal: His son Yong, crossing the river became inspector of Jiaozhou and leader of the right guard of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Yong crossed south to serve as inspector of Jiaozhou and commander of the heir’s right guard.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historical appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: editors’ appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：武帝覽觀四方，平章百姓，永言啟沃，任切爭臣。

translations.literal: The history clerk says: Emperor Wu surveyed the four quarters and balanced assessment of the hundred surnames; ever speaking of opening and fertilizing, he entrusted a cutting task to ministers who contend.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor Wu surveyed the realm and weighed the welfare of the people; longing for frank counsel, he charged his remonstrating ministers with a heavy trust.

sentences.zh: 傅玄體強直之姿，懷匪躬之操，抗辭正色，補闕弼違，諤諤當朝，不忝其職者矣。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan embodied the posture of forceful straightness, cherished the integrity of not being for himself alone, resisted in words with upright countenance, mended omissions and aided against error; forthright in court, he did not disgrace his office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan was rigid and upright, selfless in devotion, spoke his mind with stern dignity, and strove to mend faults at court—he did honor to his office.

sentences.zh: 及乎位居三獨，彈擊是司，遂能使台閣生風，貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: When he reached office among the three independents and impeachment was his charge, then he could make the bureaus catch a new wind and noble in-laws draw in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held one of the three independent censorial posts and wielded the power of impeachment, the ministries stiffened with discipline and the great families pulled in their claws.

sentences.zh: 雖前代鮑、葛，何以加之！

translations.literal: Even the Bao and Ge of former dynasties—how could one add beyond them!
translations.idiomatic: Even Han’s Bao Xuan and Ge Ying would not have surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 然而惟此褊心，乏弘雅之度，驟聞競爽，為物議所譏，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yet only this narrow mind lacked breadth in magnanimous demeanor; abruptly hearing rival brilliance, he was mocked by public opinion—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet his narrow temper lacked easy magnanimity; quick to bristle at rivals, he earned public ridicule—a pity.

sentences.zh: 古人取戒于韋弦，良有以也。

translations.literal: The ancients took warning from leather and bowstring—truly there was reason.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients took both the soft leather and the tight bowstring as their teachers—how true that remains.

sentences.zh: 長虞風格凝峻，弗墜家聲。

translations.literal: Changyu's manner was concentrated and stern; he did not let the family reputation fall.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian’s manner was grave and austere; he did not shame his father’s name.

sentences.zh: 及其納諫汝南，獻書臨晉，居諒直之地，有先見之明矣。

translations.literal: When it came to his accepting remonstrance at Runan and presenting writings at Linjin, occupying a place of honesty and straightness, he had foresight indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed his advice on the king of Runan and sent his memorials from the Linjin command, he stood in the place of blunt loyalty and showed real foresight.

sentences.zh: 傅祗名父之子，早樹風猷，崎嶇危亂之朝，匡救君臣之際，卒能保全祿位，可謂有道存焉。

translations.literal: Fu Zhi, son of a renowned father, early set his course; in a court rugged with peril he righted ruler and minister at the crisis, and in the end could preserve rank and stipend—one may say the Way was in him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, son of a famous minister, showed his quality early; through a time of coups and chaos he steadied sovereign and subject and kept his honor and salary—clearly the Way lived in him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鶉觚貞諒，實惟朝望。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Chungu's steadfast loyalty—truly a pillar of the court.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The baron of Chungu, steadfast and true, was indeed the court’s moral backbone.

sentences.zh: 志厲強直，性乖夷曠。

translations.literal: His will was stern with straightness; his nature ran against easy breadth.
translations.idiomatic: His will was fierce and upright; his temper turned away from easy-going tolerance.

sentences.zh: 長虞剛簡，無虧風尚。

translations.literal: Changyu was stern and simple, without loss to conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xian’s stern simplicity never betrayed the family’s standards.

sentences.zh: 子莊才識，爰膺袞職。

translations.literal: Zizhuang's talent and insight—then bore the robes of office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, styled Zizhuang, matched talent to insight and shouldered the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 忠績未申，泉途遽逼。

translations.literal: Loyal deeds not fully declared, the road to the springs pressed suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: His loyal service was cut short; the road to the grave came all too soon.
